full_judgment:
2. The facts, in short, are that the respondent Md Abu Bakar joined Government service as Circle Officer on 13-6-1977. Thereafter, on 15-1-1984 he entered into Cadre Service. While he was Thana Magistrate, Muladi in the District of Barisal he was selected for training in the BCS academy at Shahbagh and he joined the training course on 26-2- 1989. The training course continued up to 7-6-1989. On 8-6-1989 the HSC Examination under the Jessore Board started in Muladi College Centre. Mr Abdur Rouf, Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate, First Class, Barisal Sadar was deputed by the Deputy Commissioner, Barisal by an order dated 5-6-1989 to be in charge of Muladi Examination Centre. After completion of the training course the respondent returned to Muladi on the night following 10-6-1989. On 11-6-1989 when Mr Abdur Rouf was in charge of the examination center there was some trouble in which the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Mr Babul Mazumder was assaulted by some miscreants. At that time the respondent was in his office doing his normal duties. When he heard hue and cry from the examination center he rushed there, arranged medical treatment for Mr Majumder and directed the police to open fire when the mob attacked the residence of the UNO. He also promulgated prohibitory order under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and lodged first information report being Muladi Ps Case No.3 An Inquiry Committee constituted by the Deputy Commissioner, held enquiry into the incident and submitted report on 2-9-1989 with the recommendation to transfer the respondent elsewhere and accordingly, the respondent was transferred from Muladi. 

 4. The respondent then filed AT Case No. 144 of 1995 before the Administrative Tribunal which was dismissed by judgment and order dated 9-7-1998. The learned member of the Administrative Tribunal held that Article 116 of the Constitution was not applicable to this case and, as such, for imposition of punishment upon the respondent no consultation with the Supreme Court was necessary. He also held that the impugned order of punishment was passed after observing all necessary formalities in the proceeding. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order Appeal No. 66 of 1998 was preferred before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal which was allowed on consideration of the evidence and the deposition of the witnesses. Hence is this appeal. 

 8. We have considered the submissions made at the Bar and perused the materials on record. From the materials on record it appears that the respondent went on training during the relevant period and, as such, Mr Abdur Rouf, Assistant Commissioner and Magistrate, First Class, Barisal Sadar was deputed by the Deputy Commissiorier, Barisal by an order dated 5-6-1989 to be in charge of Muladi Examination Centre and after completion of the training course he returned to Muladi on 11-6-1989 when Mr Abdur Rouf was in charge of the examination Centre and that coming to know that there was excitement in the area and the Upazila Nirbahi Officer was assaulted by the mob who had taken shelter in the Administrative building the respondent went there and then the officer-in-charge of the police station and principal of the college and others were waiting and that an examinee was injured in the clash who died on the day, then the mob gheraoed the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and others and the respondent appearing at the scene promulgated order under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and ordered the police to open fire and the police fired blank shots and then the mob dispersed and the respondent lodged first information report with the police station on the occurrence. 

 13. It does not appear that the respondent was not a Magistrate exercising judicial function at the relevant time. Moreso, in exercise of the judicial function he promulgated prohibitory orders under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, ordered police to open fire and the police accordingly, fired blank shots and thus dispersed the unruly mob.
